newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent steady to firmer, Shell news supports.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent steady to firmer, Shell news supports.

text.p: May Brent futures were steady to firmer in late SIMEX trading on Thursday, finding temporary support from growing cut backs in Shell crude output in Nigeria.
May was last traded at $19.30 per barrel, up one cent from London which settled at $19.29 for a loss on the day of 25 cents. June was up three at $19.35.
NYMEX crude maintained a weaker stance in follow on from New York, with May last traded on ACCESS down seven cents at $20.57 per barrel.
Brokers said the ample supply of physical crude globally was continuing to weigh down on futures prices.
But headlines showing Shell output has now been cut by 210,000 bpd and it might have to declare force majeure sparked some players to cover shorts.
However, the volume was thin, SIMEX brokers noted, with May turning over just 50 lots and June 26 lots by 1000 GMT.
